results.quote: There is a deterministic comparison-based algorithm that, given a sequence S of `insert` and `delete-min` operations on an initially empty heap, computes the (unordered) list of elements remaining in the heap after the execution of S in O(|S|) total time.

There is a data structure that can execute an online sequence of n heap operations of the form `insert`, (silent) `delete-min`, `find-min`, and `reveal-deletions` in O(n+d log k) total time, where d is the number of `delete-min` operations and k is the number of `find-min` and `reveal-deletions` operations.
The mputs problem with n jobs can be solved in O(n) time.

results.bound: insert, find-min, and reveal-deletions in O(1) amortized time; silent delete-min in O(\log k) amortized time
results.quote: There is a deterministic data structure, the sync heap, that supports the operations `insert`, `find-min`, and `reveal-deletions` in constant amortized time and silent `delete-min` operations in O(log k) amortized time, where k is the number of `find-min` and `reveal-deletions` operations up to the current moment.
